chapter: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
title: The Catskills job: packing the Safari Room at Club Neverly
summary: Years later a friend got him a job in the Catskills, where the hotel manager promised to pay him if his small group, with Claude Hopkins on piano and Marcus Foster on drums, could fill the empty Safari Room.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, so I said okay, now, I don't know how long I stayed with him after that. I don't think it could have been very long, because knowing Herman, I was saying nobody will mess with my money, you know, so later on in years, after I left Pats, and after I'd finished a lot of things, I got somebody -- oh, a friend of mine told me about this job in the mountains.

In the Catskills, yeah, and at the Club Neverly, Kenny Davenport, to be positive, exact, his -- part of his -- some parts of his family, I think his mother, worked there, and secretary to this main man, the big boss, and he knew about this job, and asked me if I wanted it, and sent me up to take it.
So when I got in touch, and they -- everything went fine. So the man told me, this manager, told me, McClosky's manager, I never talked to him then --
He owned it, yeah, and the guy told me,

said we have a room here, it's the Safari Room, African room, said we've never had a -- said it's a million dollar room, it's never been packed. He said if you come in here and can pack this room, say you can write your own ticket.

Now they had 12 or 13 piece band down onstage who played for the acts, chorus girls acts, or whatever they were, you know, when we came in, and you look up where it would be the spotlight up there, that's where the Safari Room could sit there and look down on the people, and it was a beautiful room with all kind of African gadgets, and things, and hanging all on the wall, you know, this stuff.
Yeah, all that stuff, that you would find -- would find in Africa, and skins, and stuff, you know. Statues.
Anyway, I said well okay, so we started working, and we were playing in that room, and we started packing them in, and in a few days everybody was coming in to hear us, and about four pieces.

Piano, well, when I get ready to come up I'd ask him would he come up with me, and I told him, I said well who have you got on the group? I said well I've got so and so and so and so. I had Claude Hopkins. Claude Hopkins would go on piano. I said yes, and I had drummer,
Marcus Foster on Drums, hmmmmm, ah, trying to think of who did we have on -- Herman Autrey on trumpet. And so the four would finally get down, three pieces, and who the hell did we have on bass?
